speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Throughout history, the mastery of technology has been essential for a nation's progress and its ability to compete strategically.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: This importance has only heightened in the modern era.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Hence, by investing in critical infrastructure, innovation and talent development, countries can position themselves as leaders in emerging technologies and shape the future of the global economy and geopolitical landscape.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Singapore, as a small and open economy, does not aspire to be a superpower but we too must invest so as to overcome productivity challenges, unlock new economic potential and do good for our people.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Disruptions brought about by such technologies are happening more frequently and quickly.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Amidst key digital developments, artificial intelligence (AI) is now taking centrestage.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: In the book, "The Coming Wave" by DeepMind founder Mustafa Suleyman, he argued that the coming decade will be defined by a wave of powerful, fast-proliferating new technologies and AI is central to this wave.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Some of the breakthroughs in AI took place in an unexpected manner and accelerated progress significantly.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: So, we must be prepared for a future in which AI is pervasive in almost all aspects of our lives.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Yet, AI, if left to develop irresponsibly, could bring about significant harms too.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Hence, the task of maintaining human control over powerful technologies is an essential challenge of our time.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: While that sounds ominously frightening, technology is but a tool – good or bad depends on who wields it.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Given this shift in belief, Singapore needs to invest even more in digital infrastructures, talents and capabilities critical to Singapore's next bound of economic development and do more to preserve and enhance digital trust as well as leveraging digital capabilities to build communities and better lives.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: As I had articulated in my speech during the January Motion on "Building an Inclusive and Safe Digital Society", building infrastructure ahead of demand is important to maintaining competitive edge and Singapore has always done so.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Likewise, as we march on towards a smart future in the age of AI, Singapore needs to double down on our investments into higher speed networks and higher performance computing power.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Given how critical infrastructures are to deliver essential services and drive innovation, the importance of digital security and resilience cannot be undermined as they not only ensure business continuity, but also shape public confidence.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: As I had highlighted again in my January's Motion debate speech, with the likes of DBS' repeated digital service disruptions in 2023, Central Provident Fund savings lost to Android malware scams and personal data breaches in public healthcare.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Even if the incidents were no direct fault of the enterprises or institutions, these incidents would have affected significant portion of our population and, in turn, affect public's trust in digital.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Regulations are effective in setting boundaries and making clear the Dos and Do nots.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: As technologies and especially as AI evolve, regulations will have to play catch up.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: But regulations alone will not be sufficient to address these issues.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: In relation to this, the Government launched the Chief Information Security Officer or CISO-as-a-Service last year.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: The Government has introduced initiatives, such as small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) Go Digital programme in 2017, various enterprise grants over the past decade or so and implemented Industry Transformation Roadmaps that are regularly updated.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Larger enterprises are perhaps savvier and better placed to leverage such initiatives.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Some perhaps do not even need to tap into them.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: But for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), they often lack resources and expertise to select digital solutions that could enable them to improve their productivity.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: So, even with grants and solutions made available to them, they run the risk of either not employing digital solutions that are beneficial to them or undertaking digital solutions that might not be relevant to them; thereby incurring unnecessary costs and transition risks.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: The Government introduced Chief Technology Officer or CTO-as-a-Service in 2021 to help SMEs transform.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Into the third year now, how has this service fared so far?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: What else will the Government do to better help SMEs adopt digital solutions that are relevant to their business needs?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Now that half a year has passed, could the Ministry give an update on the implementation of the plans within the Blueprint and share what preliminary results that we may have observed so far?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Thirdly, we need to ensure our people are ready for what is to come.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: We are well aware of the opportunities and challenges that come with the new technologies and in this case, AI.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I spoke about it in my past speeches in this House and my hon colleagues have also expounded the merits and issues surrounding AI several times before and I believe later as well.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Some managed to get absorbed into other firms given the tight labour market.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: In talent development, education is important as it provides us with the foundation from which we build new knowledge and skills to keep up with new developments.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: We need opportunities for our young and our talents to meet other bright minds from outside of Singapore to exchange ideas and spark off new ones.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling, you can take your four remaining cuts together.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Fourthly, for the vision of a smart and digital future to be fully embraced by the whole-of-society, we must ensure that we use technology to bridge gaps, build communities and better lives.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Much was said about scams and how we must combat it to preserve social trust in a digital age during the January Motion debate so I would not repeat it here.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: What I would like to highlight is the danger of misinformation.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: In my cut to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) yesterday, I spoke of how certain messages could be spread with an intent to create schisms between Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: But there could also be other harms associated with misinformation, such as discouraging vaccinations against what could have been severe but preventable diseases.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Therefore, having trustworthy public service media channels that are accessible to all demographic groups is important in combatting misinformation and maintaining a common space that is safe for all citizens.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Hence, what is the Government doing to ensure that our Public Service Media continues to safeguard our social cohesion and common space and continues to reflect our societal values, such as multiculturalism?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Also, in fostering greater understanding and building communities, citizens of all ages and backgrounds must be able to communicate with each other.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: The ability to deliver accurate and reliable information in different languages is imperative if we are to continue engaging our seniors and various communities.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Hence, what is the Government doing to preserve our vernacular capabilities and how is the Government leveraging the ever-improving technology to do so?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: As emphasised in the January's Motion debate, a whole-of-society effort is needed.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: How then will the Government facilitate greater citizen involvement and participation in identifying problems and co-creating successful digital solutions?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Singapore will have to be ready for what is to come by investing ahead of time, preserving and strengthening digital trust and leverage digital capabilities to bridge gaps, build communities and better lives.

text: Over four Ministerial Statements in this House, the Government has put out its reasons for making the taxpayers subsidise the running of SPH Media Trust or at least, partly subsidising the running of SPH Media Trust.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: There have been recent media headlines: "Youth committed series of sexual offences involving multiple victims, including minors"; "Eight weeks’ jail for voyeur who filmed female colleague using toilet"; "Teen admits to sexually assaulting his two younger sisters multiple times"; "A 12.3% increase in voyeurism cases from 2022 to 2023: one of five things the Singapore Police Force wants us to know from their recent annual crime brief".

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I could go on, but Members would be well aware of these recent high profile headlines.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: To better understand this, I asked to speak with some youth sexual offenders some time ago.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I separately spoke to three young offenders at length, spending about an hour with each of them.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The three I spoke to came from diverse backgrounds, but not all had challenging family situations.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Based on what they shared with me, one commonality struck me: how each of them struggled with addiction to the consumption of sexually explicit materials.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: To be sure, we are talking about anecdotes from the experiences shared by three individuals.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While this is by no means representative, one also should not simply wave this revelation away.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The pervasiveness of digital technology has opened new avenues for exposure to and consumption of sexually explicit materials, especially ones of a violent nature.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While I do not claim a direct causality between pornography use and juvenile crime, extensive research has shown that adolescents' pornography use is related to more sexual aggression, both in terms of perpetuation and victimisation.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The use of online pornography has also been linked to youth self-development and beliefs, influencing one's internalisation of appearance ideals and body surveillance.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Simply put, sexual offending as a consequence and endpoint is just the tip of the iceberg.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Pornography addiction, for instance, while not actually manifesting in a crime in most instances, can continue to plague an individual's life, damaging relationships, disrupting daily routines.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is akin to a persistent, low-grade fever, symptomatic of a slew of deep-seated problems, which if left untackled can leave potentials untapped and productivity flagging.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Society pays the bill in the form of a weakened family institution and in the most extreme scenarios, an increased rate of perverse and violent crimes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With the high internet and social media adoption rates in Singapore, it is high time that we paid much closer attention to online harms and the widespread spillover impacts it has on society at large.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: On a separate but related note, unrealistic body standards paraded on the internet fuel a mindless pursuit of perfection and external validation.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I admit I personally feel some pressure to stay in the right shape.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, I sometimes hit the gym after midnight, determined to squeeze in a workout before the end of a long day.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, I am almost always surprised by the fact that I always have company at the gym by the number of young people, most of whom are young men, who remain seriously committed to sculpting their bodies even at unearthly hours.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Yes, for as long as we can remember, traditional media like the big and small screens – that is, film and TV – has led the charge in peddling unrealistic body standards.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, the proliferation of social media and the democratisation of content creation has only intensified peer comparison and hyper-fuelled unrealistic expectations of our own body image.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Simply put, the need to be that perfect bod is as real as it gets.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Much of the conversation thus far, frames body image insecurities as a women's issue, but we know that is far from the truth.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Men too face pressures and in the process, are actively discouraged to acknowledge or share about their own insecurities.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: At its core, we need to begin a conversation on what masculinity means in Singapore society today.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I recently chanced upon an article on NPR.org and I thought would like to leverage its content and run a little thought experiment with Members in this Chamber today.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope many of you are listening to me.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am going to read out three pairs of descriptors and Members can decide for yourself, which set of descriptors, either the former or the latter, more aptly describes what it means to be masculine.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The first set: expressing anger over expressing sadness.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The second set: swearing that we are fine even when we are actually not versus reaching out to loved ones and trusted friends when in need.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The third set: laugh in the face of fear and danger versus being vulnerable about thoughts and feelings.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In your opinion, Members of the Chamber, which group better describes masculinity?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: You do not have to make known your position or your answers to me, much less take a vote on this – you do not have to reach for the buttons.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope this simple exercise illustrates the effect of stereotypes at work.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Admittedly, this is a difficult conversation to have.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: To some, even talking about redefining masculinity is perhaps effeminate and even emasculating.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We are increasingly seeing arrangements that go against the strand of what traditional masculinity looks like: stay-home dads who step into primary caretaking roles; dating down where the woman in heterosexual relationships has a higher earning power, all of which come with their challenges and stigma to tackle.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Rounding back, the concerns I have expressed on online harms and its impact on society, especially young men, is something we collectively need to tackle: from Government, community, families, parents and that is a work-in-progress.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But at the heart of it all, we also need to have a mindful dialogue on what it means to be man enough in today's context.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With almost a third of Queenstown's residents age 60 and above, we have implemented several programmes and municipal enhancements to ensure that seniors can age well in place.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For instance, the hilly terrain and wide roads of Mei Ling Street and Stirling Road pose a safety concern for seniors when they cross the roads.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: To enhance safety and to allow seniors the respite of a brief pitstop, the central dividers between have been widened, amongst other enhancements.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These include mental health programmes like SafePod, workshops on future care planning and a Seniors' Festival that is currently in the works.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This Festival aims to empower our seniors, show them and their family members that one does not have to fear ageing and that there are many ways through which one can still enjoy their golden years.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: At the Active Ageing Centre at Mei Ling, they will be launching the Gym Tonic, a strength training programme that tracks seniors' fitness and progress using senior-friendly gym machines.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Despite the many programmes that we have put in place for our seniors, one persistent pain point they face is catching up with technology.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: One constant feedback that I hear from seniors is the need for automated teller machines (ATMs), especially those with the passbook update function.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many shared with me that having to travel a distance away to the next nearest ATM is of great inconvenience to them.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is especially so when they are less mobile.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I feel their pain when they narrate their challenges to me.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Despite the proliferation of digital banking, many seniors I spoke to still preferred transacting in cash.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Some have expressed unfamiliarity with digital banking apps; others feared being scammed.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Understanding their concerns, I have appealed multiple times to our banks although I have not always been successful.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While some seniors are hesitant, I take heart in the fact that many of them remain open to learn how to go digital and pick up tips on how to stay safe online.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: That is why I am appreciative that Leng Kee Community Club (CC) – located within Queenstown – has been designated by the SG Digital Office (SDO) as a SG Digital Community Hub.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: SG Digital Community Hubs were initiated by IMDA as part of Singapore's digitalisation push and are conveniently located in various parts of our heartlands.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The hub at Leng Kee CC is open daily from 10.00 am to 6.00 pm.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Seniors get one-on-one guidance in a customised fashion to equip them to go digital.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The Seniors Go Digital Activity Pack gamifies the learning experience and encourages seniors to continue learning on their own with online resources.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Given Singapore's rapidly ageing population and Queenstown's super-aged resident profile, SG Digital Community Hubs would become more important in equipping seniors and seniors-to-be for digital life as technology continues to evolve.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In addition to the Community Hubs, the Mobile Access for Vulnerable Seniors is another scheme that has been implemented in recent years.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It provides subsidised smartphone and mobile plans to lower-income seniors who want to go digital but cannot afford them.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In addition, our seniors are also encouraged to step up and pick up a basic digital skill at our Community Hubs.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As we continue to equip our seniors for the digital age, technology can be harnessed to preserve a sense of emotional connectedness.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Through an app, VintageRadio.sg aims to build confidence in seniors to explore an unfamiliar digital world by evoking a sense of familiarity as they do so.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These tunes and presenters will be familiar to many of our seniors and having them as company makes the digitalisation journey hopefully a little less intimidating.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: At this juncture, I would like to compliment the VintageRadio team for providing one more important channel through which our seniors can stay digitally as well as emotionally connected.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, for colleagues in the Ministry, my final question is this: what then is our uniquely Singaporean-infused water recipe?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Jessica Tan, please take your four cuts together.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: AI and GenAI have the potential to transform industries and improve our quality of life, reimagining the way we live and work.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: AI development and deployment are however, not without risks, such as bias training data or algorithmic design, privacy concerns with the analysis of large amounts of data, the complexity and sometimes, the lack of transparency of AI systems.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: There are also concerns with security risks with the sophisticate use of AI to exploit vulnerabilities in systems.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Despite the risks, GenAI and machine learning with capability to learn from large amounts of data efficiently can predict potential cyber threats and secure systems.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: For Singapore, the strategic bets are to leverage AI to address big challenges, such as population health and climate change.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: How will we be able to develop capability and enable improved productivity and competitiveness of businesses and Government with AI and to prepare our workforce, especially our lower-skilled workers, that will be disrupted by the use of AI to reskill and to be prepared for the opportunities?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: How will we address and minimise the risks of AI?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Mr Chairman, technology is important but without having people to imagine what is possible with technology and capable of utilising, developing and innovating with technology, we would not be able to realise the potential and value of technology.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: These were the findings of a report in 2021, commissioned by Amazon Web Services, amongst six Asia Pacific countries.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: With the push for digitalisation not just in Singapore, but around the region as well, there will be increased competition for talent.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: How will we ensure that we build the capability, grow and retain the talent and skills required to support our digital ambitions and growth?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: With the pervasiveness of technology and digitalisation, including AI, we can expect every job role to be redesigned in some shape and form.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Most jobs will need some form of digital literacy.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: How can businesses be supported, especially less digitally-ready SMEs, to develop digital capabilities to improve productivity and competitiveness?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Mr Chairman, in Singapore, with rapid technology development, the push to digitalise and the greater use and reliance on digital technologies is very much a part of how businesses operate and how people work across many sectors.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: For individuals, digital is very much a part of life – from our social interactions, buying and paying for goods and services to leisure and entertainment.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: With the increasing reliance on digital for how we live, work and play, how will the Government foster a trusted digital environment, resilience and security of Government services and the responsible use of digital technology, including AI?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: How will we assure our people of service availability, protection of their personal data and the security of their digital transactions?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: How is the Government ensuring that Singapore's digital infrastructure remains secure and resilient so that businesses can have the confidence to do business digitally and offer their services seamlessly, reliably and securely?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Mr Chairman, the vision of our Smart Nation is, "a Singapore where people are more empowered to live meaningful and fulfilled lives, enabled seamlessly by technology, offering exciting opportunities for all." At its core, the Smart Nation is about people and making lives better.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The Smart Nation objectives are to improve the everyday convenience and the quality of life of Singaporeans, drive greater business effectiveness and value and support new areas of innovation and ensure that no one is left behind.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Hany Soh, you can take your two cuts together.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: (In Mandarin):   According to last year's Singapore Digital Society's Report, more Singaporeans are using digital skills in their daily lives.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Among them, the most significant progress is in the use of mobile applications for payments and internet browsing by the elderly.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: However, there is still a need for improvement, in understanding and using new technologies.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many elderly residents in Woodgrove have also expressed to me that while they acknowledge the benefits of digital technology in their daily lives, they feel almost powerless to keep up with the rapid developments and transformation of these digital technologies. : Chairman, getting the buy-in of the entire nation to embrace digital transformation is an incredible task.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While the advantages of digitalisation are universally recognised, there are some who remain reluctant to adopt it.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Having listened to my Woodgrove residents, I gathered that many seniors face difficulties keeping up in the nation's progress towards digitalisation.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For most of them, learning with a patient and personal touch is much more preferred and effective.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As we continue to introduce new technologies, we must first understand the needs of the end-users and the overall user experience as well as ascertain the most effective modes of imparting the knowledge and skills for operation.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Mr Chairman, every third Saturday of the month, many of my Woodgrove residents enjoy bringing their little ones to our Woodlands Regional Library – where their children aged four to six years partake in a fun-filled afternoon, listening to engaging stories and participating in book-based activities, such as crafts and quizzes.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Events like these that are meticulously planned by the National Library Board (NLB) are greatly appreciated and many of my residents have shared their feedback with me that they hope to see more similar events happening in the community, even outside the library.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In this regard, I understand that MOLLY, NLB's mobile library services may be able to fulfil such wishes.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank all Members for their cuts.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A decade ago, we launched the Smart Nation initiative, with the vision for Singapore to be a nation where people live meaningful and fulfilled lives enabled by technology, offering exciting opportunities for all.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There is no doubt that technology has become a big part of Singaporeans' daily lives.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Overall, 84% say that digital technologies have made their lives easier and more than half are prepared to try new technologies.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In January, Parliament debated extensively on a Motion on digital inclusion and safety.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For the Committee of Supply (COS) therefore, MCI will cover three other important aspects of Smart Nation development.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: First, leveraging technology to uplift our collective potential.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: During the Budget and Committee of Supply debates thus far, no fewer than 15 Members of Parliament have mentioned AI developments in their speeches.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong pointed out, AI is a general-purpose technology that will find many applications, some of which we cannot yet imagine.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But it is not the only type of technology Singapore has invested in.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, we have also built capabilities in quantum technology.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Nonetheless, given the current strong interest in AI, I will expand on the Government's plans to strengthen the AI ecosystem in Singapore and guard against its risks.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Last December, we launched our refreshed National AI Strategy (NAIS 2.0), as one of the key planks of our Smart Nation effort.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It builds on investments made under our first National AI Strategy that was launched in 2019.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MCI agrees with Ms Mariam Jaafar that our AI ambitions should not be driven by hype.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While we have invested to build Sea-Lion as a means to grow our capabilities and test the hypothesis that that there is value in training large language models (LLMs) on Southeast Asian languages, we have avoided headlong competition with builders of big frontier models which cost much more.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Like Ms Mariam Jaafar, we believe that Singapore's interests are better served through the deployment of use cases, based on the most suitable foundation models that can be developed anywhere in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Among other goals, NAIS 2.0 aims to create new peaks of excellence in leading economic sectors and areas aligned with our Smart Nation priorities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Later, Senior Minister of State Dr Janil Puthucheary will also update Members on plans to boost the infrastructure that powers AI activities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will focus on talent development and governance.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the world of AI, we can think broadly of three communities: AI creators, who generate cutting-edge AI research, design frontier systems and drive novel use cases; AI practitioners, who have the skillsets to implement and deploy AI systems, models and algorithms in organisations; and AI users, who are equipped to use AI-powered solutions and services, increase productivity to take up better jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Every city with some AI ambition wants these creators, practitioners and users – as many as they can get.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The competition is extremely intense, as alluded to by Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Sharael Taha.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Take Dr Koh Pang Wei for example – an award-winning AI researcher who is currently based at the University of Washington.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Dr Koh is highly sought after because he focuses on building AI models that can work with imperfect data, which is a common problem in real-world applications.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: During the COVID-19 pandemic, Dr Koh developed novel methods to estimate the movements of people from raw data.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This led to models that helped governments understand the spread of the COVID-19 virus and inform reopening policies around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Dr Koh is a born and bred Singaporean.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As much as we would like him to come home, we also recognise the value of the networks that he is plugged into because of his current appointment.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In fact, there are other researchers like him from diverse nationalities who would like to work more with us.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We welcome them and will soon launch a new AI Visiting Professorship for world-class AI researchers to collaborate with Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will also partner AI Singapore and our universities to launch a new AI Accelerated Masters Programme to grow our pipeline of Singaporean AI researchers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Practitioners include data scientists and machine learning engineers and who develop and translate the use of AI in organisations across the economy.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Take the example of SG Digital Scholar Mr Joshua Wong.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The SG Digital scholarship gave Mr Wong the opportunity to study computer science in Cambridge University, gain exposure to AI research and build networks with some of the best global talent in AI.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This helped him to fulfil his dreams to be an entrepreneur.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In 2020, he co-founded Hypotenuse.AI, a startup which provides an AI-powered platform for businesses to create marketing content in seconds.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Today, Mr Wong continues to enjoy networking opportunities with fellow scholars and mentors younger talent.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will support more young Singaporeans with similar aspirations as Mr Wong.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Beyond students, we will also support recent graduates and mid-career workers who wish to become AI practitioners.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: IMDA plans to scale up the TechSkills Accelerator, or TeSA.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It will provide funding support to employers with relevant career openings to induct and equip locals through upskilling opportunities and industry-relevant training.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In parallel to efforts to grow the creator and practitioner communities in Singapore, we will equip the broader workforce to be confident AI users.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This may be the best way to forestall AI-induced job displacement which many Members, including Mr Yip Hon Weng, have expressed concerns about.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As with previous waves of technology proliferation, workers worry about being replaced.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With AI, it is not just rank and file workers, but professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) who feel at risk, that AI tools and agents can take over the tasks that they currently perform.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These include knowledge-based tasks, like research, coding and writing.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Many thoughtful observers have, however, pointed out that it is not so much AI displacing the workers, but AI-proficient workers displacing AI-deficient workers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While we cannot fully predict the scope and scale of AI disruptions, these JTMs provide useful signposts for employers, unions and workers, so they can plan for job redesign or training interventions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Consequently, many of the NTUC's company training committees refer to them.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Agencies responsible for sector development can also identify suitable training interventions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, the IMDA appointed five training partners under the Information and Communications JTM in September last year.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As of December, they have trained about 1,000 people to be confident AI users.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There will be thousands more in the next three years.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This year's Budget has also provided a generous top-up to SkillsFuture Credits and the Level-Up Programme for mid-career Singaporeans looking to reskill through full-time diploma programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: IMDA will work with SkillsFuture Singapore to ensure that there are suitable offerings to help more of our people gain AI-proficiency and stay relevant in the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And, as suggested by Mr Gerald Giam, we already go beyond training programmes to promote hands-on learning.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A very good example is the NLB's MakeIT programme, which allows participants to try their hand at 3D modelling and printing, robotics and coding.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The public sector itself provides both formal and informal learning experiences to build AI capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, we have introduced tools like Pair, our secure version of ChatGPT, to help public officers in tasks, such as writing, brainstorming, research and coding.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Today, around 35,000 public officers use Pair in their work to improve their productivity.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This means ensuring that businesses continue to grow, including through the use of technologies like AI.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: By doing so, we need not react passively to job displacement by AI, but proactively use AI to reinstate better jobs for our people.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why we will also invest in promoting AI adoption among enterprises, a topic which Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How will deal with later.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While we welcome opportunities that come with AI advancements, we must also guard against the risks of misuse.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, AI can intensify existing threats, such as cyber-attacks, scams, or misinformation and disinformation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza, Mr Xie Yao Quan and Mr Mark Lee asked what we are doing to promote safe and responsible uses of AI and how we will protect personal data that may be used to train AI models.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At COS last year, I outlined our plan to clarify how the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) applies to AI systems.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: PDPC will next consider giving guidance on the use of personal data to train generative AI (GenAI) systems.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr de Souza asked how MCI will continue to place Singapore at the forefront of AI governance.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Indeed, Singapore has been recognised as an active and credible contributor to AI Governance.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Last year, we launched the AI Verify Foundation, to harness the expertise of the global open-source community to promote responsible use of AI.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This builds on the roll out of AI Verify, a testing framework and software toolkit, in 2022.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Today, the Foundation counts organisations, such as IBM, Google, Deloitte, DBS and SIA as members.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the World Economic Forum in January this year, we announced a Proposed Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI (MGF-GenAI), and sought views from our partners.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This framework builds on the earlier Model AI Governance Framework and reflects emerging principles, concerns and technological developments in GenAI.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: More recently, Singapore led the development of the ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics, which was endorsed at the fourth ASEAN Digital Ministers' Meeting held here last month.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will now move on to the second theme of my speech: upholding trust in the digital domain.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Both Ms Hany Soh and Mr Eric Chua asked how we maintain the human touch, amidst increasing digitalisation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The reality is that there is no silver bullet.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Digitalisation is taking place across multiple settings and changes our interactions with each other in so many ways.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will, therefore, have to feel our way forward and be willing to adjust our approaches.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Where the Government is concerned, we are mindful that the delivery of public services through digital means should be carefully designed to cater to different population segments, including seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Two days ago, Minister Chan Chun Sing also reiterated the Government's commitment to ensure that our services remain accessible to all.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, citizens who require support for Government services can head to any ServiceSG Centre, which can help with close to 600 services and schemes from over 25 agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: IMDA's Digital Ambassadors also stand ready at multiple community touchpoints to provide guidance to seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As the digital landscape evolves, our libraries will also continue efforts to promote reading and lifelong learning.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This includes NLB's mobile library service, or MOLLY, which Ms Hany Soh touched on.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is obviously very proud of these achievements and will certainly continue to reach out to as many as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I should also add that it is not only MOLLY that brings the library to our citizens, there are other ways in which the library makes its presence felt.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, there are pop-ups stations in busy shopping malls and other locations with high foot fall, and you will find some representation of the library in them.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will now address two other dimensions of digital trust that Ms Tin, Ms Jessica Tan, Mr de Souza and Mr Xie asked about: security and resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These largely concern the digital infrastructure and services that power our digital economy and enable citizens to meet their day-to-day needs.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In 2023, Singapore faced disruptions in online Government services, banking and payment services, and when accessing the websites of public healthcare institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Many countries are grappling with similar issues as they become more digitalised.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, a data centre outage in France caused widespread disruption to government and other services.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A cloud service outage in the US caused many websites to be inaccessible, including those of news outlets and airlines.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To manage the impact of such disruptions, the EU, Germany and Australia have already introduced regulations to enhance the security and resilience of digital infrastructure, such as cloud services and data centres.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While we cannot fully eliminate disruptions, we will do more to minimise their occurrence.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: An inter-agency task force led by MCI has been reviewing the evolving landscape and developing mitigating measures.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The expanded coverage will include data centres, cloud services and key entities that may hold sensitive data or perform important public functions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While enhancing our cybersecurity posture is important, it is not enough.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Past outages in Singapore and elsewhere have shown that disruptions can occur due to non-cyber reasons.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These include misconfigurations in cloud architecture or the outage of data centres due to fires, water leakages and cooling system failures.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The DIA will focus on digital infrastructure that can cause significant impact on the economy and society if disrupted.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, large cloud service providers and data centres are crucial to the functioning of a wide array of digital services that enterprises and consumers use daily.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These operators may, therefore, need to meet higher security and resilience standards, to reduce the likelihood of systemic disruptions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The task force is conducting further studies to properly scope the DIA and develop its proposals.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The challenges are complex and include the cross-border nature of digital infrastructure operators, like cloud service providers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will also need to balance trade-offs between mitigating risks and increasing compliance costs.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will continue to consult industry players and relevant stakeholders, and ensure coherence in requirements between the DIA and the Cybersecurity Act.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Second, the task force is exploring non-regulatory measures that will complement our laws and regulations.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These could include providing guidance to digital infrastructure and service providers on best practices for security and resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While the Government does our best to ensure that digital infrastructure and services are secure and resilient, enterprises and consumers also need to play their part.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, enterprises must have robust business continuity and incident recovery plans.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Smaller enterprises can refer to resources like the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore's (CSA's) Cyber Essentials programme; larger enterprises should adopt CSA's Cyber Trust mark.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Consumers should also be prepared to use alternatives if a digital service disruption occurs.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This creates a strong incentive to service providers to buck up.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Xie asked about the risks associated with quantum computing – especially in our data and communications networks.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Last June, Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat announced the launch of the National Quantum Safe Network Plus (NQSN+).

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are also building capabilities to develop solutions that enable safe and trusted data sharing – something that Ms Mariam Jaafar talked about.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In July 2022, we launched the Privacy Enhancing Technology Sandbox Initiative to support businesses in piloting technological solutions that allow them to safely extract value from data whilst protecting personal data and commercially sensitive data.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mastercard was one of the participating businesses which piloted a solution to share information on financial crime across international borders while complying with prevailing regulations.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mastercard is now studying the implementation of this in a commercial setting.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I now turn to the third and final theme in my speech: safeguarding our infrastructure of fact to uphold social cohesion.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Internationally, we have witnessed how deepfake technology has been misused to spread falsehood and manipulate public opinion on gun violence in the US; the Israel-Hamas conflict and even undermine election integrity.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Their realism makes them a particularly dangerous weapon, as pointed out by Mr Christopher de Souza, Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Eric Chua.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We take a strong stance against malicious AI-generated content.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Targeted legislation to deal with them swiftly is thus one pillar in this infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This includes the Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act, which enables us to issue corrections and label AI-generated misinformation with the correct facts.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We can also consider disabling directions if the content poses serious harm to public interest.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Another pillar is public education initiatives to equip Singaporeans to be discerning consumers and producers of information.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our libraries play a key role in this effort.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Last year, NLB introduced resources and workshops on GenAI as part of its S.U.R.E programme to educate Singaporeans about the benefits and perils of AI, as well as impart skills to verify and fact-check online content that may be AI-generated.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Later this year, NLB will roll out new programmes and learning packages to educate Singaporeans about the risks that AI-generated misinformation can pose to society.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We also recognise the need to grow new capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We previously announced that MCI and the Agency for Science, Technology and Research will launch the Centre for Advanced Technologies in Online Safety (CATOS).

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In a fragmented media landscape awash with AI-generated content, audiences are finding it very difficult to separate truths from falsehoods.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We therefore also need trusted news media to inform and engage our people, to keep us all on the same page.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Pritam Singh asked about Government funding to SPH Media.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As a public service media entity, SPH Media plays a crucial role in: informing Singaporeans of issues of national importance; reflecting Singapore's values and way of life; reporting international events with a Singapore eye; and projecting Singapore's perspectives to the rest of the world.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SPH Media is also an institution and repository of our shared memories.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Last year, Lianhe Zaobao celebrated its 100th Anniversary whilst The Straits Times is approaching 180 years of publication.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Both Berita Harian and Tamil Murasu are also well-established, catering to the needs of our Malay and Tamil language communities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, SPH Media is facing its biggest challenge yet.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The entire media industry has been severely disrupted by digitalisation and social media.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Readership is declining as audiences have a multitude of choices.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Traditional sources of revenue are also falling dramatically, with advertising shifting to social media and other online platforms.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These problems are not unique to SPH Media.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even an established media company like The Washington Post lost US$100 million last year and had to cut 10% of its headcount, despite extensive efforts to transform.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Pulitzer Prize-winning BuzzFeed News shut down last April, despite hiring top journalists and opening bureaus around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: According to The New York Times, one out of four newspapers that existed in 2005 no longer does.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Prior to restructuring into a company limited by guarantee, SPH posted its first ever loss.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Left to market forces and commercial stresses, it would likely have gone the way of The Washington Post and BuzzFeed.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is particularly so with its vernacular titles, which have naturally smaller audiences and which members like Mr Sharael Taha and Ms Tin are rightly concerned about.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is reflected in MCI's Budget Book, as part of MCI's overall grant disbursement provided to other organisations.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As I shared previously in the House, funding for SPH Media is targeted at three main areas: talent, technology and vernacular capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They reflect the importance the Government has placed on quality journalism, digital transformation and upholding multiculturalism.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To ensure public accountability and fiscal prudence, SPH Media Trust is structured to comprise members representing different segments of society – from commercial entities like DBS, UOB and OCBC; to local institutes of higher learning like the National University of Singapore, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore Management University and Singapore University of Technology and Design.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But ultimately, SPH Media is accountable to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The news industry is a people-centric business and SPH Media has a crucial public service media role.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Therefore, KPIs are set to track reach and engagement across all communities, including specific targets for the vernacular outlets, youth and digital reach.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MCI also requires SPH Media to report regularly on their performance in these areas and comply with relevant audits to ensure oversight of how funds are spent, as well as ownership and accountability of public service media outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So far, the funding disbursed has been put to good use.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SPH Media has been strengthening its digital systems to improve its outreach, in line with what other global publications have done.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal, for example, have pivoted from print to digital-first models, adopting multimedia formats to increase their readership.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Likewise, SPH Media recently adopted a new digital content management system to support its online coverage and launch mobile apps across its English and vernacular news titles.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It has also made extensive efforts to improve retention and quality of its newsrooms through training, scholarships and fellowships with overseas institutions, such as the Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, there is still considerable catch-up for SPH Media.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: More importantly, these results show that the efforts made thus far are just the beginning.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SPH Media will need to do more to maintain its relevance in this challenging media environment and will need continued support as it strives to get onto firmer footing.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, I hope Members agree that in an information landscape where truths have to compete with falsehoods, public service media is a critical pillar in our society's infrastructure of fact.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: On matters deserving public attention, such as critical global events, community news in the vernacular; or indeed, Parliamentary proceedings, profit-driven platforms may have no interest except to sensationalise or add their own spin.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We also need public service media to tell Singapore's stories and project Singapore's voice.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We cannot expect media organisations elsewhere to do so for us.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At stake is our ability as a people to have a shared understanding of issues of the day, to know where our national interests lie and what we must do to ensure our continued success.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Sustained investment in our public service media entities is therefore, not a nice to-do; rather, it is a have-to-do if we are to uphold quality journalism that supports the public good.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I therefore seek Members' support to sustain public investment in public service media entities to preserve our infrastructure of fact and maintain the high trust that our public has in public service media today.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, with your permission, please allow me to conclude my remarks in Mandarin, returning to the topic of AI which I started with.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: (In Mandarin):   AI will continue to permeate various regions and sectors worldwide including Singapore's society and economy.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We must seize the opportunities to help our people and businesses prepare.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To this end, I have announced several initiatives today.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: First of all, we will launch a new programme to attract the world's top AI creators to come to the Lion City and collaborate with local experts and scholars to establish cutting-edge technologies in our country.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government will also invest $200 million to cultivate local talents, providing them with scholarships and opportunities for overseas internships.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, while digital technology brings opportunities, it also brings risks.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Therefore, we will introduce new guidelines governing use of personal data in AI systems.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government is also exploring a new law to enhance the security of our country's digital infrastructure and services, ensuring that people can use digital technology with greater peace of mind.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I have always been advocating for "digital first, but not digital only".

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government will continue to provide non-digital options for citizens who are not yet ready to go online.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, the momentum of AI development will not slow down.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr Chairman, we have made good progress in digitalising our economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, more than nine in 10 enterprises are using e-payment today, compared to just six in 10 in 2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Enterprises are also deploying more advanced digital solutions, such as cloud computing and data analytics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Importantly, I am heartened that our SMEs are doing so too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As of November last year, 60% of our hawkers accept SGQR digital payments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The platform has facilitated an average of 5.1 million transactions or $42 million per month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: IMDA's programmes like SMEs Go Digital and Hawkers Go Digital have moved the needle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: At the same time, the pace of technological advancements, especially in AI, is picking up pace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We want to equip our enterprises and workers with the capabilities to ride this new wave.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are developing a Digital Enterprise Blueprint to chart the next bound of our effort, which Mr Xie Yao Quan has asked about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have been consulting extensively with sector partners and industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are refining the Blueprint, based on their feedback, and will put out a consultation paper in the coming months to seek views from the wider industry and from the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: But let me take the opportunity to outline the broad contours of the Blueprint.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Digital Enterprise Blueprint is a live document, which will be continually updated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Hence, we have started to implement some "no regrets" moves that received broad support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ms Jessica Tan, Ms Tin Pei Ling, Mr Sharael Taha and Mr Mark Lee and others asked how we are supporting SMEs to benefit from AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will help enterprises and workers access benefits from AI capabilities through IMDA's SMEs Go Digital programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: First, for the vast majority of SMEs, IMDA curates a list of pre-approved digital solutions suitable for broad-based adoption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have started working with the technology industry to incorporate AI capabilities in their digital solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I am glad to share that as of today, around 20% of these pre-approved solutions are already AI-enabled.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, AI capabilities are integrated seamlessly into customer relationship management solutions which help enterprises analyse customer interactions and data to suggest personalised marketing campaigns for customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: So, that is for the broad base of SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Second, at the sector level, IMDA has worked with sector leads to co-develop industry digital plans (IDPs) which serve as roadmaps for enterprises, highlighting solutions which meet specific needs of the sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Today, we have 22 IDPs for various sectors, including sectors like wholesale, construction, retail and food services, and these IDPs cover a broad swathe of our economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: IMDA will refresh the IDPs to incorporate AI-enabled solutions that would be relevant to meet the needs of the enterprises in that sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have started doing so in the four IDPs that we either launched or refreshed last year, namely legal, tourism, retail and security sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: One good example, I met a company, Ghows LLC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: It is a law firm that has been using an AI-enabled proofreading tool to help check their draft contracts for conflicts and inconsistencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I understand from lawyers that this process used to be done manually and was tedious, time-consuming and error-prone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: After adopting this AI-enabled tool, Ghows saw a 50% productivity improvement and less errors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will progressively refresh all IDPs to include sector-specific AI solutions so that enterprises can benefit from these useful solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ms Tin asked about the CTO-as-a-Service, over 92,000 users have accessed resources from the CTO-as-a-Service platform and over 1,600 SMEs have benefited from the digital consultancy services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: One example is food services company, Xi Men Jie (西门街).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The company was overwhelmed by the numerous technology solutions in the market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The team turned to a digital consultant under the CTO-as-a-Service scheme for help to integrate their digital systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The company achieved 15% in both manpower savings and sales growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: So, I encourage all SMEs to tap on these schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For enterprises who want to do more, we are supporting them through our Advanced Digital Solutions (ADS) scheme, which brings together the technology ecosystem to curate solutions for key problems identified by the sector leads.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We launched two new schemes under the ADS for enterprises to gain experience using GenAI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The first scheme is a programme by IMDA and EnterpriseSG to provide a pilot group of SMEs with access to 13 specially curated GenAI solutions for common business functions like marketing and sales.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: If these GenAI solutions prove useful, we will include them in the SMEs Go Digital pre-approved list of digital solutions to benefit others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And for the second scheme, it is for larger and more digitally-mature enterprises who are looking to develop and deploy their own GenAI digital solutions in their businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are heartened to see early interest from enterprises and we welcome more to sign-up for these initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
