text: In our consultations, SMEs shared that as they started to grow, they realised that they were constrained by lack of interoperability and scalability of their digital solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, Bread Createur, a food services SME, had adopted various sales channels and delivery platforms over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: However, they found themselves unable to collate orders automatically and track sales figures across their third-party delivery platforms and sales channels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: What was an inconvenience for a small operation, quickly turned into a showstopper when they grew.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Where integrated solutions are not available in the market, we will curate such solutions through the ADS scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: One example is the Connected Business Suite solution available to Food Services SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: It enabled these SMEs to operate their frontend and backend functions in an integrated manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: With this integrated solution, Bread Createur, which I mentioned earlier, can easily track all their sales and transactions across different sales channels, including from third-party orders that are routed directly to the kitchen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Going forward, we will work closely with sector leads and associations to introduce more pre-approved integrated digital solutions and cloud-based solutions to support our enterprises to scale quickly as they grow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And integrated and scalable digital solutions would also require the sectors and enterprises to redesign their processes and operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I am heartened to see that in CSA's latest cybersecurity survey findings, 75% of organisations were aware of the importance of cybersecurity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: However, while enterprises are taking steps to improve their cyber hygiene, there is still much room for improvement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: CSA also found that only one in three organisations implemented more than half of the five categories of cybersecurity measures under CSA's Cyber Essentials Certification Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Lack of knowledge on how to implement cybersecurity solutions, was commonly cited as a challenge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ms Tin and Mr Xie asked how are we helping SMEs to then improve their cyber resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: While we will flesh this out in the Digital Enterprise Blueprint, let me give Members a broad sense of our three-tier approach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: First, we will support SMEs in taking steps to improve their cyber hygiene.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will launch a cybersecurity health check tool for enterprises so that they can assess their cyber hygiene, benchmark themselves against their industry peers and access resources for them to plug the gaps.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Those who require more support can tap on the CISO-as-a-Service scheme to engage cybersecurity consultants to develop tailored cybersecurity health plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Second, we will go upstream and raise the cybersecurity standards of the digital systems used by our enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This will especially benefit SMEs with no inhouse cybersecurity resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will start with the pre-approved digital solutions under IMDA's SMEs Go Digital programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Third, we will also work with sector leads to develop industry-specific guidelines for cybersecurity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In healthcare for example, CSA worked with the Ministry of Health to develop cybersecurity guidelines to improve the cybersecurity posture amongst healthcare providers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: So, Mr Chairman, I spoke briefly about the three thrusts of the Digital Enterprise Blueprint to uplift enterprises and workers in the Age of AI by being smarter, scale faster and becoming safer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: At the broader workforce level, more of us will need to be equipped with the right skills to effectively use digital tools in our work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: With more rapid technological changes, we need to see reskilling and upskilling as part of our workplace culture and see this as a continual investment in ourselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Employers must also view the reskilling and upskilling of their employees as investments, so as to fully benefit from the digital systems that have been put in place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: An analogy would be like having a very powerful car but not being able to go beyond the first gear.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We need to upskill our employees, so that we can make full use of that more powerful engine.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: That is why each IDP does not only include a suite of curated digital solutions for enterprises, but also comes with a comprehensive list of relevant training courses for these digital tools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, the retail IDP includes courses for employees to learn how to make good use of social commerce solutions to generate more sales – including how to sell items on livestreams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: IMDA has also worked with SkillsFuture Singapore to provide funding support for many of these courses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: So, I encourage employers and workers to make full use of these schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Sufficient quality and quantity of tech talent is also crucial to realising our ambitions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Understandably, there have been concerns about prospects in the technology sector, given the layoffs by technology companies, as mentioned by Ms Tin.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Technology companies across the world have been right-siting and right-sizing their operations to prioritise new areas of growth, amidst a more challenging economic climate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Unfortunately, this sometimes results in layoffs which can be very painful and distressing for those involved.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Singapore is no exception and has similarly seen some layoffs by technology companies which have largely impacted those in non-technology roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Fortunately, Singapore remains a key node in many of these technology companies' global strategies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As they deepen and expand their involvement in the region, demand for technology talent in Singapore will continue to grow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This was driven by demand from both the information and communication sector and non-information and communication sectors, with the latter accounting for around 57% of technology jobs in 2023.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As more companies adopt digital, including using more advanced digital solutions like AI, we expect that this will also fuel demand for tech talent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: A case in point, university graduates of information and digital technology courses continue to take home the highest median monthly starting pay at $5,500 a month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ms Jessica Tan, Ms Tin Pei Ling, Mr Alex Yam and Mr Sharael Taha have asked about how we will ensure a steady pipeline of tech talent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are also working hard to strengthen Institute of Technical Education (ITE) and polytechnic graduates' employment outcomes in tech and provide more development pathways for them throughout their careers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We set up TeSA for ITE and Polytechnics Alliance (TIP Alliance) in 2022 to bring together like-minded partners – school leadership, tech industry associations and leading employers of tech manpower like NCS, Accenture and ST Engineering – to come together to drive change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I am heartened that employers are changing their mindset and human resource (HR) practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Instead of just looking at academic qualifications, employers are giving sufficient weight to the applicants' skills and capabilities to assess their suitability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: To push for change across the industry, IMDA and the TIP Alliance launched the Skills-Based Hiring Movement, together with a handbook providing practical guidance for firms to attract, assess and develop tech talent based on competencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Oracle is an example of a company that has pledged its support for skills-based hiring and has been recruiting based on skills for their openings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As part of their commitment, their recruitment team has chosen not to highlight the education requirements in their job postings for all technical roles in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The skills-based hiring approach aligns with the shifts that we are making as part of Forward SG to embrace learning beyond grades and create diverse pathways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For instance, in respond to industry feedback, the Information and Digital Technologies (IDT) schools in our ITE and polytechnics have lengthened internship durations from six to 12 months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Last year, more than 400 of such polytechnic and ITE students undertook year-long internships to gain greater industry experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will support companies which provide these year-long internships, by providing co-funding to cover the cost of training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Ms Queenie Ng is a beneficiary of this programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: While at Ngee Ann Polytechnic, she embarked on a year-long internship with OCBC as a full stack developer, working on dashboards and architecture projects to improve operational efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Queenie found the scale of the projects to be an eye-opener.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: In contrast to the smaller-scale school projects, the internship exposed her to more complex systems and their interconnections.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: This experience expanded her understanding of the dynamic tech industry and the many exciting career options it has to offer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: (In Mandarin):   Sir, AI is taking us further down the digitalisation path.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Besides bringing competitive advantages to our businesses, it also enhances the productivity of our workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: More importantly, we will collaborate with various industries to plan relevant training courses and assist workers in mastering skills, staying updated and seizing the new opportunities brought by AI. : Sir, Singapore does not have the natural advantages of many other economies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We do not have a sizeable domestic market, large local workforce to tap on, natural resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: But we can well punch above our weight by being agile and making full use of technological enablers like digital and now AI, to continue enlarging market opportunities for enterprises and creating good and exciting jobs for Singaporeans and we are building on a very strong foundation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Government will be a steadfast partner for enterprises and workers in the next phase of our digitalisation journey to uplift enterprises and workers in the age of AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: So, I welcome more like-minded partners to work together with us and invite all our enterprises and workers to join us on this exciting journey ahead.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Members for their cuts and their questions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, I would like to take the opportunity to explain MCI's approach towards Digital Government: how we need to create and are creating effective digital products, being citizen-centric by looking at Singaporeans' needs by experimenting and embracing experimentation and how we are investing in digital infrastructure and research and development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: All these, so that Singapore is well-equipped to realise our Smart Nation ambitions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our most successful products are the result of asking the same question: what challenges do Singaporeans face?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This lets residents claim and spend Government-issued digital vouchers, including the CDC vouchers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It has been a key enabler in our shift away from paper vouchers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The drawbacks of paper vouchers for the consumer are obvious.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The paper vouchers received had to be bundled together daily, then collected, manually processed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Simple effective digital products can have a tangible impact on people's lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked how the Government can facilitate greater citizen participation in identifying problems and co-creating successful digital solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Sharael Taha also asked how the Government can continue to better Singaporeans' lives through new digital products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Build For Good is a good example of how we do both.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This brings together volunteers to build digital solutions for fellow citizens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One of the teams tackled the problem of student counsellors having to spend time writing case notes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Their solution is a product called the NoteFlow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is a tool for transcribing and summarising case interviews and counsellors can then focus on caring for their students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: NoteFlow and other promising ideas coming out of Build For Good are prototypes and we are hopeful that some of them will mature in time and make their own contribution to the public good.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Having identified the problem, we explore different solutions to tackle it: build prototypes quickly; test them out with real users; and scale the ideas which show promise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The problems the Government has to tackle are challenging, and trying different things to figure out what works best is our best bet to solve these problems for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The ideas that we experiment with, as I have described, multiple approaches to a single problem means that some of the ideas that we experiment with will not work out.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The team had observed that it is sometimes difficult for hawkers, especially elderly hawkers, to visually check for proof of an e-payment on a customer's device.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, having identified this problem, within a couple of months, a small team from GovTech had built a "proof-of-concept" prototype for MoneySound.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is a device which reads out incoming digital payments so that the hawkers' hands are not occupied and they do not have to look to then check this digital payment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We tested it with the hawkers but we found out that they were not keen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Come up with an idea, move quickly, establish through "proof-of-concept" whether it is likely to be well-received and, if it does not, we have to press pause.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is disappointing when these ideas do not work out as expected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But this is the process of experimentation that our Digital Government engineers are working through.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But the insights from such an approach are useful and they will help us to tackle the next problem or the next iteration of the product.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This experimentation approach also allows us to try multiple strategies at the same time to tackle big problems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For instance, GovTech teams have been exploring how to help citizens access relevant information from Government websites.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Providing the right information for citizens in the right way is a big problem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Instead of searching for a single silver bullet, we have launched several products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Each targets a different segment of users to address different needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Singaporeans in need of assistance can use SupportGoWhere.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is a one-stop portal to find Government schemes or funded services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One of its key features is the Care Services Recommender for caregivers to find care services, financial support schemes and future planning tools suited to their circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This enables them to find support conveniently, instead of having to navigate various Government websites in search of relevant information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They do not need to know where to go to find the relevant information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But sometimes, if there is a need for more general information, so we produced another product, SearchSG, which is a search engine that uses AI to provide citizens with relevant up-to-date search results scrapped from a variety of Government sources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, multiple strategies and try to solve the same problem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In doing so, we are able to learn about the needs and experiences of our users as they engage with our digital products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And the faster we learn, the faster we improve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ms Jessica Tan asked how the push for digitalisation has improved Singaporeans' lives as the Smart Nation initiative enters its 10th year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Allow me to share some of the key strategies that we are applying, that we think have resulted in this improvement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One is that we have to work to improve the day-to-day lives of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Third, in doing so, we have to be more inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: If I could, perhaps, share some examples in each of those categories.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are many digital services available through websites, app stores or other channels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are also needs that the market does not address or finds it difficult to address.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One example of this and it keeps Singaporeans safe from scams is ScamShield.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is difficult for there to be a market solution that can adequately protect Singaporeans in quite the same way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is one of our most wide-reaching tools in the fight against scams and I would encourage Singaporeans to use it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Second, is offering better and more integrated Government services and a couple of examples here.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Users can easily make appointments for vaccinations, for screenings, such as mammograms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This product is available in English, Mandarin, Malay and Tamil.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Again, that is an aspect of the service that is difficult for the market to solve in the way that we need it to, in multiple languages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This product also allows users to see what subsidies are applied to their health appointments from schemes, such as the Community Health Assist Scheme and MediSave.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And so, we are bringing together two or three different aspects of the service the market is unlikely to do – an appointment scheme provided in multiple languages and so that you can see the subsidies that you would get for these appointments at the time to help you make your decision.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It brings together reliable information and digital services related to end-of-life planning as well as post-death matters in a convenient portal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is difficult, even for those of us who have thought ahead.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These times of our lives do not happen very often; a lot of stress, a lot of uncertainty and a lot of things to get done, a lot of services and transactions that we need to get done.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, every bit of support helps at a time like this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One example of this sort of experience is Mr Christopher Hamzah.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: He is married, he has got a four-month-old daughter.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And back in 2021, Mr Hamzah saw first-hand the challenges his close friend faced in settling his late father’s affairs in the midst of grieving.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Learning from this experience, Mr Hamzah and his wife decided to start planning early and turned to MyLegacy for help.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With the MyLegacy product, Mr Hamzah could easily record important details – his various accounts, his insurance policies – and share that information with trusted persons.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: He describes the portal’s dashboard as intuitive, very easy to use and navigate, and he takes heart from the assurance that this information would not be used for third-party marketing, and he has become an enthusiastic advocate for MyLegacy among his friends and family.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Again, I would encourage Members to look at the MyLegacy product and encourage their residents and constituents to consider signing up for it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The third part of our strategy is to be more inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Eric Chua had some questions about this and brought up some points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: He asked about the mobile phone access of our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chua also spoke about the need to better support seniors in general to navigate the digital space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And to do this, we launched the Seniors Go Digital programme, and over 280,000 seniors have been trained so far.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: At the same time, we also have to take efforts to be inclusive in our design and development; take the process to our seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We test our digital services with a wide range of users, including seniors, to ensure that their needs are met.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have also built tools specifically to support those with differing needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One example, and Members can try this out for themselves at Level 1, is a product called “ReadLiao”.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is one of the prototypes that emerged from our recent Hack For Public Good hackathon.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, seniors sometimes struggle with long and complicated letters and often have to rely on caregivers, including children, to summarise the information for them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Those with older relatives might be familiar with the experience of looking at these letters, explaining such letters to them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is often not just the language but also how the material is presented.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, ReadLiao uses Optical Character Recognition together with an AI platform, repackages and displays documents in a clear and comprehensible format to better communicate the content to seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We intend to pilot ReadLiao within the community in the coming months and hopefully build it into a full-fledged product.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is literally only a few weeks’ old, at the prototyping stage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have another tool which is more mature.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is called “Purple A11y”, GovTech’s open-source, automated testing tool.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It scans webpages and it identifies potential accessibility issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Developers can use it to identify improperly labelled buttons or images.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For most of us, these are things we do not notice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These are not necessarily errors that we pick up and we do not see the difficulty that such a design might present.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But if you are visually impaired, if you use a screen reader to navigate digital services, getting this type of design correct makes a huge difference.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Since 2023, we have used Purple A11y to make Government digital services more accessible, and it has been directly integrated into the development for websites like MyCareersFuture, to ensure that they are accessible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But there is another aspect to the work that we have to pay some attention to – the infrastructure, the interconnected systems that must work together to make such products even possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Sharael Taha asked how MCI is equipping Singapore to make the most of latest technological developments, especially in AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ensuring Singapore has the foundational infrastructure to power AI activities is vital.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We envisage that these resources will support use cases across sectors, such as financial services, healthcare, transport and logistics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And over time, we hope for this seed funding to catalyse greater development and the use of AI in Singapore and spur additional industry investment in compute infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling asked about plans to implement the Digital Connectivity Blueprint.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Launched last June by MCI and IMDA, the Digital Connectivity Blueprint (DCB) outlines Singapore’s strategy for building the next generation of our digital infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It covers various infrastructure components – the hard infrastructure like submarine cables which connect us to the world; the middleware that links diverse systems, applications and devices for them to work together; and many other factors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The DCB is about integrated master planning to ensure we have what we need, when we need it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And over the next few years, we can look forward to seeing the DCB’s bold ideas come to life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, one of the DCB’s strategic priorities is to enable seamless 10 giga bits per second (10G) domestic connectivity within the next five years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are setting aside funds to enhance the capacity of our Nationwide Broadband Network (NBN) to make such 10G broadband a reality.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Like with the NBN back in the 2000s, we are investing ahead of demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan asked how we can power our digital future more sustainably.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As mentioned in the Budget Speech, the Energy Efficiency Grant (EEG) will be extended to the data centre industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With the rollout of the EEG to the data centre industry by the end of 2024, we hope more data centre operators and end-users will adopt energy-efficient equipment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: EEG is just one of several efforts to grow our data centres sustainably under the Green Data Centre Roadmap, which IMDA will be launching later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Beyond the products, beyond the infrastructure, we also need to make sure we have access to the right technologies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Singapore needs strong research and development capabilities to develop and tailor technologies for our local context.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Launched last September, the Programme Office serves as a coordinating body to spearhead Singapore's efforts in translating research into commercial solutions for Government agencies and the industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is a key enabler to both strengthen our digital security and grow our digital economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Sharael Taha also asked how MCI is building Singapore’s research capabilities in AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Over the last five years, we have invested more than $500 million on AI research, and our investments have borne fruit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We rank among the top 10 countries based on publications at top AI conferences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our researchers have won international accolades, such as the Google AI PhD Fellowship, which recognises about 50 graduate students worldwide each year for their exceptional and innovative research work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In addition, we have supported close to 150 research collaborations with Government and industry partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Some big projects, some small, some in areas that you do not expect, such as AI Singapore working with a dental chain, Q&M, to help dentists detect diseases from X-rays, perform automated dental charting and recommend dental treatment plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I recommend all Members to have their teeth regularly checked, with AI, if necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With access to the newest technology becoming increasingly necessary to attract investments, we must continue to invest in R&D to maintain our competitive edge in the global market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Digital technology is one of our most powerful tools to meet the needs of citizens and businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We embrace bold development and agile experimentation so that we can wield this digital technology to create the greatest possible impact for Singaporeans and for Singapore.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: When we saw the upgrade happening in 2006, we did see quite a few residents not signing up.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: So, as you talked about the half a million expected to sign up, I hope that there will be good communication to residents and businesses to ensure that they do sign up for it and not miss the cycle.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: And we just saw so much logistic challenges there.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: So, I hope that there will be a lot of communication to ensure that people understand what to do and when to sign up, so that we do not see a repeat of that.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Indeed, a new product and a transition to a new – it may or may not be a new business model, depending on what the operators do – and we have to make sure that we adequately communicate this to the consumer base.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, her point is well taken and we will certainly follow up on that.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: On the first point with regard to the question I asked on the specific line item in the Budget Book, which would essentially flesh out the funding to SPH Media Trust, and I thank the Minister for pointing out that it is under "Grant Subventions and Capital Injections to other Organisations".

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I say this because, in view of the funding framework and how the Government has stepped in into the public service media space, if I can call it that, I think it will be helpful for people to track, on an ongoing basis, how much taxpayer funding goes into the funding of SPH Media.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: That is just a suggestion for the Ministry.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, that is just something for the Minister to consider and I would be grateful if she could comment on that, please.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mr Singh for his suggestion.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think it is not entirely up to MCI to decide how these things are reported in the Budget Book because there is a certain convention that the Government follows.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I do not recall exactly, but my impression is that say, you take public transport subsidies, for example.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I do not believe it is reflected in the Budget Book as line items that it goes to SMRT; it goes to SBS Transit; it goes to another bus operator.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Certainly, I think if you consider the funding for preschool services, I do not recall that it also goes down to entity level.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is just we provide for a cluster of activities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We do not necessarily reflect in the Budget Book exactly what sums go to which entities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I could be wrong, but it is certainly something that we will look at.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But it is not entirely up to MCI how to show these things in the Budget Book.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the Budget Book, we report on the KPIs that the Ministry is required to meet.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, for MCI, we are responsible for IMDA.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: IMDA has got interactions with telecoms companies (telcos).

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We may not provide funding to them, but we license them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They are also very critical service providers in Singapore.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They also have KPIs to be met in order to continue to hold their licence.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It does not mean that we lock, stock and barrel, transport the KPIs into the Budget Book.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is quite a different way of representing the scope of our responsibilities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think his broader point is that the public would benefit from more information about how these entities, the public service media entities are doing.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will have to find more ways of putting information out that is reasonable.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I would, however, add, Mr Chairman, that we can continue to look at things like reach, readership, engagement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But if we come back to the fundamentals of why we are supporting public service media, it goes back to the question of whether Singaporeans have media sources that they can trust.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is trust that is the most important.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think in that regard, at least the Reuters Institute, which Mr Singh himself mentioned, does have an annual report that is quite useful.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It looks at, amongst media organisations, the most trusted brands in Singapore.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Singh cited the findings of 2021, where he said that The Straits Times, which is one of the titles belonging to SPH Media Trust, came in at 77%, I believe.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think, if I could just say how useful that report is in helping us to shape our own thinking.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The latest report that has already been made available is of 2023.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are left with the BBC, which is a UK company.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If you then use that as a lens of thinking about why and how we should continue to resource our own public service media, I think in some sense that beats all the indicators that we can put in place.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I am not saying that those KPIs are not important.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think they have to be continuously evaluated together with other kinds of validation which Mr Singh himself highlighted.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: On the same note in relation to KPIs, I also strongly urge MCI, in terms of the KPI considerations, we should look at several factors, notwithstanding that certain KPIs are unfortunately not met due to the existing circumstances.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: We should also focus in terms of other priorities, emphasising perhaps on other KPIs' importance in terms of, for example, what the Minister has said on public trust.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: To me, another very important critical factor to also take into account is branding.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: For example, brands like The Straits Times and Lianhe Zaobao – how it relates back to our Singapore's brand and identity, reflecting to the outside world of what is exactly happening in Singapore, inviting for more foreign investors to come to Singapore.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: These are the good avenues and ways where we want to reach out to the outside world.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Chairman, I fully agree with Ms Soh.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In management speak, we like to say what gets measured gets done.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, there is a certain interest in ensuring that there are KPIs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But within MCI, we ourselves are fully cognisant that it does not fully reflect what we need our public service media entities to achieve.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The standing that they enjoy in the world is not entirely measurable.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The identity that they help to foster among Singaporeans, the unity, you also cannot quite put a number to it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we are constantly in discussion with our public service media entities on whether there are better ways to reflect their progress.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, Ms Soh's points are very well taken.

speaker: The Chairman
text: It looks like there are no more clarifications for the Minister and the two Senior Ministers of State.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Could I invite Ms Tin Peh Ling, if you would like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: With so much to do, Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
